correctness.rationale: For n>=2 the seven mutually disjoint defender-count cases exactly partition the 0/1/2-labellings; necessity and sufficiency follow from neighbor sets excluding the matched index. Their closed terms sum to the stated polynomial. Standalone standard-library exhaustive enumeration of 597861 assignments for n=2..6 matches all coefficients, and exact polynomial arithmetic checks boundary and minimum coefficients through n=30. The infinite proof is combinatorial, not computational.

evidence: A public complete-multipartite total Roman enumerator covers only complete multipartite graphs; the crown graph for n>=3 is not complete multipartite, since nonadjacency is not transitive.
Theorem 10 of arXiv:2005.13608 classifies products at minimum weight <=7, rather than all feasible weights.
broader_coverage.reasoning: On a crown graph distinct same-part vertices are nonadjacent and matched opposite-part pairs are also nonadjacent, but other cross-part pairs are adjacent: nonadjacency cannot define equivalence classes for complete multipartite structure. The general minimum theorem cannot give the many independent high-weight coefficients.

originality.rationale: Four claim-versus-prior comparisons identify no covering whole-weight crown total Roman theorem. The strongest 2020 primary proof gives optimum-weight classification only, not nonoptimal coefficient counts; the near full enumerator concerns complete multipartite graphs, which do not contain the crown family for n>=3. Specific equivalence and database searches were completed with indexed-record limitations explicitly retained.
residual_risks: Unindexed, differently named, or very recent literature may contain an equivalent crown all-weight identity.
Two relevant published semantic-record summaries, not their complete public source files, were inspected; their described graph/condition distinctions are decisive for the comparison presented.

value.rationale: Full weight enumeration of every total Roman function on the natural family K_2 tensor K_n is a stronger counting invariant than the known minimum. The deleted matching produces a seven-regime decomposition, and the formula determines an entire degree-4n polynomial for every n, including exceptional small-order behavior. It is not an arbitrary finite restriction or restatement of a general optimum bound.
